idiom_name: pure mapping functions returning plain objects (toDto / fromDto); JSON or structuredClone only for representation copies
implementation_notes: JavaScript's idiom is a pair of pure functions in one module - `const toDto = (u) => ({ id: u.id, name: u.fullName })` and `const fromDto = (d) => new User(d.id, d.name, d.is_admin ?? false)` - which is the mapper object of the classic pattern dissolved into two functions; a mapper class is a transliteration and buys nothing here. Keep the functions free of I/O and of instance state, and let the module boundary do the isolating: only this file imports both the API shape and the domain type. `JSON.parse`/`JSON.stringify` (or `structuredClone`) copy the representation, not the meaning - they do not rename fields, restore prototypes or fill defaults - so a domain class whose methods the boundary needs must be rebuilt by the mapper, never by copying the parsed object.
pitfalls: Object spread copies enumerable own properties only: class getters, private #fields and non-enumerable members vanish silently, so read through accessors explicitly.
structuredClone discards the prototype chain and throws on functions or DOM nodes, so cloning a domain instance does not produce a domain instance.
A missing field becomes undefined rather than an error; decide per field whether undefined means absent, default or invalid, and normalise at the boundary once.
Deeply nested payloads are shared, not copied, so a mapped object can still mutate when the source JSON is transformed later.
